title: 1. Understand what AI is (and what it is not)
goal: You know how language models work, where they get things wrong, and what you must not give them.
items: A language model predicts the next word – it does not 'know', it generates. That is where hallucinations come from.
Context window, tokens, and how models differ (fast and cheap vs. smart and slow).
Data protection: what you may paste into AI and what you may not (personal data, trade secrets, EU AI Act basics).
Try the same task with 2–3 different tools and compare the results.

resources.title: Elements of AI (free, also available in Estonian)

title: 2. AI as an everyday work assistant
goal: You use AI every day for at least one of your work tasks and save visible time.
items: Pick 3 of your repetitive tasks (emails, summaries, documents) and do them with AI for 2 weeks.
Learn to give context: role, goal, audience, an example, the format you want.
Always check facts and numbers – your name is on the result.
Keep a short log: what worked, what did not, how much time you saved.

title: 3. Reusable workflows
goal: You have your own prompt library and projects/context files, and AI is a natural part of your workflow.
items: Build a prompt library for your typical tasks (templates + good examples).
Use projects / custom GPTs / your own documents as context (the basic idea of RAG).
Multi-step workflows: research → plan → draft → critique → revise.
Multimodality: images, spreadsheets, PDFs, voice – where does it help in your work?

title: 4. Automation and agents
goal: You have automated at least one process end to end so that it runs without you.
items: No-code: Zapier / Make / n8n + an AI step (e.g. classifying emails, compiling reports).
AI agents and tool use (MCP) – what an agent does and how to limit it.
Measuring quality: test cases and 'evals', not just 'looks good'.
Cost, privacy and security: who sees the data, how much one run costs.

title: 5. Specialize and share
goal: You are the person in your team or field who knows how to use AI properly in that work.
items: Combine your domain knowledge with AI: solve a problem that general AI cannot solve without you.
Document and share: an internal training, a blog post, a LinkedIn post about your results.
Follow the field: 1–2 trustworthy newsletters, not the daily hype.
Update your CV: concrete results you achieved with AI, with numbers.
